name: The Plane Tree of Via Santa Croce

location.address: Giardino Martino Martini, Via Santa Croce, 38122 Trento TN, Italy

transport: roughly 10 min on foot from Trento station, in the historic centre
verified_sources: MASAF national monumental trees register, sheet 15/L378/TN/22
verify_notes: The oldest of Trento's officially designated monumental trees. Three independent 2024 local-press pieces (Trentino/Giornale di Trento, ANSA, il Dolomiti) all give a planting date of 1835, framed as having 'witnessed nearly two centuries of Trentine history.' Trento's list of 18 monumental trees was formalised around 2023-2024, with 13 added to the national AMI (Alberi Monumentali d'Italia) register that year. Stands in the small Giardino Martino Martini public garden.

name: The Elm of Piazza Dante

location.address: Giardino di Piazza Dante, 38122 Trento TN, Italy
location.neighbourhood: Piazza Dante / city centre, next to the station

access: Free, public garden; comune.trento.it describes it as 'il primo giardino pubblico di Trento' (Trento's first public garden)
transport: immediately next to Trento's main railway station
verified_sources: MASAF national monumental trees register, sheet 22/L378/TN/22
https://www.comune.trento.it/Vivere-il-comune/Luoghi/Giardino-di-Piazza-Dante ('i tassi e l'olmo secolari sul lato nord', the centuries-old yews and elm on the north side)
verify_notes: The Comune di Trento's own page for the garden calls this elm 'secolare' (centuries-old), standing on the garden's north side alongside equally old yews. The garden was laid out in 1879 by engineer Annibale Apollonio on land reclaimed when the Adige was diverted for the railway (1854-58), and is described as Trento's first public garden; restored since 2007, it now hosts a children's library in a restored Art Nouveau pavilion. Directly opposite Trento's main railway station, the easiest tree in the city to reach.

name: The Elm of Maso Ginocchio

location.address: Giardino di Maso Ginocchio, Via Giusti, 38122 Trento TN, Italy

access: Free, public garden (Comune di Trento), with entrances from Via Veneto, Via G. Giusti and Via Monte Baldo
transport: roughly 15-20 min on foot south of the centre
verified_sources: MASAF national monumental trees register, sheet 23/L378/TN/22
https://ilregistrodeglialberi.it/17959-olmo-campestre-trento-tn-trentino-alto-adige (RAMI register entry for the Maso Ginocchio field elm)
verify_notes: A survivor: the RAMI register notes it has lived through Dutch elm disease, the fungal epidemic that has killed most of Europe's mature elms since the 1930s by blocking the tree's vascular system, while most other elms nearby did not. RAMI describes it as tucked in a corner of the garden but imposing once found, with a girth already above the monumental threshold (register: 393cm); no age or height recorded by either source. The garden itself is a public municipal park (about 3.6 hectares) in the San Giuseppe-Santa Chiara district, with a play area and a small animal enclosure; one 2016 local-press piece described it as under-maintained at the time, a comment on upkeep rather than access.

name: The Cedar of Parco Gocciadoro

location.address: Parco di Gocciadoro, Via Hermann Gmeiner 25, 38121 Trento TN, Italy

transport: roughly 25-30 min on foot east of the centre, or local bus to the Gocciadoro area
verified_sources: MASAF national monumental trees register, sheet 09/L378/TN/22

https://www.ildolomiti.it/societa/2024/dal-cedro-dellhimalaya-al-ciliegio-selvatico-18-alberi-monumentali-a-trento-e-altri-10-candidati-per-diventarlo-il-piu-antico-del-1835-ogni-pianta-e-un-mondo-e-una-storia (cedar in Parco Gocciadoro planted around the time of Italian Unification, ~1861, the city's second-oldest monumental tree)
verify_notes: Local press (il Dolomiti, 2024) dates a cedar in Parco Gocciadoro to roughly the 1861 Italian Unification, calling it the second-oldest of Trento's monumental trees after the 1835 Via Santa Croce plane (tre_001). The same article credits the park with a separate, taller Liriodendron (35m, the tallest monumental tree in the city, not part of this register batch), which means the park holds more than one monumental specimen; the article gives no girth to cross-check against this register entry (525cm) and does not pin the cedar's exact spot within the park, so flagged pending a tighter match. A well-known public city park regardless.

name: The Chestnut of Sardagna

location.address: Loc. Castagnara, Sardagna, 38121 Trento TN, Italy
location.neighbourhood: Sardagna (across the Adige, reached by cable car)

access: Free, public hillside area on the Sentiero dei Castagni (Chestnut Trail), reached via the Funivia Trento-Sardagna cable car or by road
transport: Funivia Trento-Sardagna cable car (about 4 minutes, 200m to 600m elevation) from the city centre, then a walk on the marked Sentiero dei Castagni
verified_sources: MASAF national monumental trees register, sheet 20/L378/TN/22
verify_notes: Register locality 'Castagnara' sits within Sardagna's chestnut grove, a hillside area above Trento reached by cable car that was made into a waymarked trail in 2025 (Sentiero dei Castagni, with the Trento-Sopramonte forestry authority and the Sardagna district), and whose chestnuts won a De.Co. (denominazione comunale) local-product mark the same year. Local coverage names other individual chestnuts in the area by their own nicknames (Castegnar della Lasta; another that famously stopped a runaway bus in January 1949), but no source found this pass confirms this specific register-mapped tree is one of the named ones, hence approximate rather than confirmed precision and flagged. Worth the trip for the cable car and hillside setting on its own merits even if the exact tree's fame is less certain than the city-centre entries.
